defects.summary: `--repin-source` advances a federated pin without ever checking that the checkout it reads is the registry the lock names, so it writes another repository's commit SHA under that registry at exit 0 — defeating the identity probe that already guards the primary's `--repin`.
defects.evidence:
scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:780-838 (`_apply_repin_sources`) checks only `path.is_dir()` and then does `resolve_ref(path, ref or "HEAD")`. `HEAD` resolves in ANY git repo, so the replacement ref is written before `plan_sources` gets a chance to resolve the OLD pinned SHA in that clone — which is what used to catch a wrong clone. The primary path has the exact guard that is missing here, at :1717 `_git(repo, "cat-file", "-e", f"{pinned}^{{commit}}")`, whose own comment says why: "when they are different repositories the re-pin writes a commit from one under the name of the other — exit 0, and --check green because it re-derives from the same wrong clone".

REPRODUCED, with NO `--source-repo` override — the default `../<repo-name>` sibling lookup alone (a fork, or a same-named repo under a different owner, cloned at `../cms-platform`). Harness: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/atk/a2_default_sibling.py
  lock pins  Adam-S-Daniel/cms-platform@dbf6241f...  (the real registry's commit)
  sibling ../cms-platform is a DIFFERENT repo, HEAD ab3499f1...
  [bare --repin]   exit=1, lock unchanged: True  -> "ERROR: cannot resolve ref 'dbf6241f...' in .../cms-platform"   <- the pre-existing guard works
  [--repin-source] exit=0  -> "Wrote ...: 2 skills from ..., Adam-S-Daniel/cms-platform@ab3499f1..."
  lock now: {'registry': 'Adam-S-Daniel/cms-platform', 'ref': 'ab3499f10d4d1b94ed8308d00e1f35846bf145e3', ...}

So the new flag REMOVES a guard the old path had. Second harness (a_wrongclone.py) shows the aftermath: `--check` from the same machine is GREEN (exit 0) because it re-derives from the same wrong clone, while `--check` against the real clone fails with "cannot resolve ref". Downstream the bootstrap hook fetches `<registry>@<sha the registry does not have>` and every consumer session reports DEGRADED — the precise failure the primary's guard exists to prevent.

No test covers this: `test_repin_source_honours_source_repo_for_an_out_of_tree_clone` relocates the SAME registry's clone and asserts it still works, which is the case that must keep passing, not the case that must fail. Fix shape: before replacing a source's ref, probe the checkout with `cat-file -e <the ref the lock currently pins>^{commit}`, exactly as :1717 does for the primary.

defects.summary: When a lock federates one registry twice (two bundles, two independent pins — representable and `--check`-green), `--repin-source 'X@'` advances BOTH entries, moving a source the caller never named. The module docstring says the flag advances "ONE of them".
defects.evidence:
scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:822-838 merges with `ref = wanted.get(source["registry"])` inside a loop over every extra, so one `--repin-source` spec matches every source sharing that registry. Nothing refuses the duplicate: `normalize_source` allows it and `plan_sources`' uniqueness check is keyed on BUNDLE, not registry.

REPRODUCED. Harness: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/atk/b_dupreg.py
  lock before (generated at exit 0, two INDEPENDENT pins on one registry):
    {registry: .../cms-platform, ref: e2a4c1fe (c1), bundles: ['cms-platform'], layout: 'skills'}
    {registry: .../cms-platform, ref: 52a73d16 (c2), bundles: ['other'],        layout: '{bundle}'}
  $ --repin --repin-source '<uri>@'   -> exit 0
  lock after:
    {... ref: 6ff07115 (c3), bundles: ['cms-platform'] ...}
    {... ref: 6ff07115 (c3), bundles: ['other'] ...}     <- moved two commits, unnamed and unasked

The `other` bundle's source was pinned at c2 and is now at c3, with its digests rewritten to c3's content. The module docstring added in this PR (scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:223-233) states "`--repin-source '<REGISTRY>@[<ref>]'` is now the one way to advance ONE of them", and `_apply_repin_sources`' docstring guarantees only "Never adds, never drops" — neither covers this.

The inconsistency is internal, not just theoretical: `_select_sources` (:1237-1290) treats the ANALOGOUS ambiguity — one registry standing as both primary and source — as a hard `GeneratorError` on the read-only path, on the stated ground that "Scoping to it has two answers, so it gets none." The write path resolves the same class of ambiguity silently, in the direction that moves more pins. Either refuse a `--repin-source` whose registry matches more than one source, or state the fan-out in the docstring and test it.

defects.summary: The new report loop's cross-repo contract comment claims the bumper's 20-line cap "can never separate a headline from the command that fixes it". It can, and does — the truncation lands on a federated `FAILED:` headline with its remediation line cut.
defects.evidence:
scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:1806-1815, fact 3: "Every headline is IMMEDIATELY followed by its own remediation line. That is what makes the 20-line cap safe: a truncation can drop a whole trailing block, but it can never separate a headline from the command that fixes it." The same absolute is repeated in the docstring of `test_every_failed_line_is_followed_by_its_own_remediation_command` (scripts/test_generate_skills_lock.py).

The arithmetic defeats it. The primary block is 5 fixed lines (headline + `--repin` + 3 note lines) plus D difference lines; the first federated headline therefore lands on line 6+D of the slice. At D == 14 that is line 20 — included — and its remediation line is line 21, cut.

REPRODUCED against the real generator. Harness: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/atk/e_truncation.py (14 primary skills drifted + 1 federated skill drifted), applying the bumper's own `sed -n '/^FAILED:/,$p' | head -20`:
  line 20 : "FAILED: file:///.../cms-platform's bundles have moved on since 18758995..."
  line 21 : "  python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --repin-source 'file:/..."  <- CUT
The PR body a reviewer reads ends on a failure headline naming a registry with no command under it.

The test does not establish the property its docstring claims: it asserts adjacency in the UNTRUNCATED stdout, and never applies `head -20`. D == 14 is the exact primary case, but the same split occurs for a second federated headline whenever D_primary + D_source1 == 12, so this is a family of configurations, not one boundary. Either make the claim conditional in the comment, or move the remediation line ABOVE its headline / add a guard the cap cannot split, and test the truncated slice rather than the raw one.

defects.summary: Both new `--only` parser guards test truthiness, so `--only ''` (an unset shell variable) slips past them; with no other flag the run silently degrades to a plain generate that de-federates the lock AND rewrites `registry` to DEFAULT_REGISTRY, at exit 0.
defects.evidence:
scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:1633 `if args.only and not args.check_current:` and :1635 `if args.only and (args.check or args.check_format):` — an empty string is falsy, so neither `parser.error` fires.

REPRODUCED. Harness: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/atk/c_only_empty.py, on a federated lock:
  $ --only 'Whatever/Repo' -o lock        -> exit 2  "--only scopes --check-current; pass it alongside that flag."  lock unchanged
  $ --only ''               -o lock        -> exit 0  "Wrote ...: 1 skills from Adam-S-Daniel/agentskills@48aab0c4..."
     sources still present: False   (DE-FEDERATED)   registry replaced with DEFAULT_REGISTRY
  $ --check --only 'Whatever/Repo' -o lock -> exit 2
  $ --check --only ''              -o lock -> exit 0  "OK: ... is current (2 skills at ...)"

The second pair is the guard's own stated failure mode reached anyway: :1635's message says such a run "answers no question anyone asked", and with an empty value it answers the unscoped question at exit 0 while the caller believes it was scoped. `--only "$REG"` with an unset REG is the ordinary route in a shell caller, which is what PR 2's bumper will be. Use `if args.only is not None` for both guards (the sibling `--repin-source` guard at :1627 is safe only by accident — argparse `action="append"` makes `['']` truthy).

defects.summary: `_apply_repin_sources`' docstring asserts that an unnamed source "comes back by reference, so it serializes byte-identically". It does not, whenever that source's stored ref is not already a resolved SHA — `plan_sources` resolves it downstream and `build_lock` writes the new commit.
defects.evidence:
scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:788-798 makes the claim; :904 `sources.append({**source, "path": path, "ref": resolve_ref(path, source["ref"])})` breaks it. `normalize_source`/`validate_ref` accept a branch name in a source's `ref`, so such a lock loads.

REPRODUCED. Harness: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/atk/d_branchref.py — lock with sources[0] pinned at a SHA and sources[1] recording "main"; `other-platform` then gains a commit nobody asked to pin:
  $ --repin --repin-source '<cms-platform uri>@'   -> exit 0
  sources[1] ref: main -> 628829e12f3a   (UNNAMED SOURCE MOVED TO THE NEW COMMIT: True), digests rewritten to the new content.

Honest scoping: d2_control.py shows a bare `--repin` moves it too, so the BEHAVIOUR is pre-existing — it is the byte-identical GUARANTEE, added by this PR and load-bearing for the merge-not-replace invariant, that is new and false. Per the house rule on comments, either qualify it ("byte-identical for a source whose ref is already a 40-hex SHA — which is all this generator writes") or make it true by carrying an unnamed source's ref through unresolved.

Same root cause, minor second symptom: `scoped_ref = ... selected[0]["ref"]` at :1801 reads the RAW lock ref, so a `--only <source>` OK line would name `main` while the FAILED path for the same source names the resolved SHA.

defects.summary: `_select_sources`' refusal text tells the operator their lock's primary and source "carry different bundles and different layouts" — but the layouts can be identical, so the message asserts something false about the lock in front of the reader and then says "Fix the lock".
defects.evidence:
scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:1268-1278. Only the BUNDLE lists are forced apart (by `plan_sources`' uniqueness check); nothing forces the layouts apart, and a source omitting `layout` inherits DEFAULT_LAYOUT — the primary's own layout.

REPRODUCED. Harness: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/atk/f_layoutclaim.py — one registry as both primary (bundle `adam`) and source (bundle `beta`), source layout omitted:
  generate -> exit 0; layouts: ['plugins/{bundle}/skills'] == DEFAULT_LAYOUT (identical to the primary's)
  $ --check-current --only '<that registry>' -> exit 1
    "ERROR: ... this lock names it as BOTH its primary registry and a federated source, and those two carry different bundles and different layouts — so scoping to it has two different answers. Fix the lock, ..."

In that shape the two entries share a registry, a layout and a ref, so scoping to it has one answer, not two — the refusal is defensible as conservative but its stated reason is not checkable and here is simply wrong. Drop the layout clause, or condition the message on what the lock actually holds.

defects.summary: Commit c4ca54f prints a `--repin-source` remediation command that the generator does not accept until commit a5af776, so any bisect or review landing on that commit gets advice that exits 2.
defects.evidence: `git log --oneline b81f6f1..HEAD` in /home/user/agentskills/.claude/worktrees/wf_f015efb1-07e-2: c4ca54f "Report a federated drift as that registry's, not the primary's" precedes a5af776 "Give a federated pin one way to advance that cannot de-federate a lock". The report's own deviation list concedes it ("at commit 2 the federated remediation names a flag the code does not accept until commit 3 — an intermediate-state wart"). Against the house rule of one logical change per commit, the ordering is backwards: the flag is a prerequisite of the message that names it, and swapping the two commits removes the wart at no cost — a5af776 does not depend on c4ca54f's attribution.

NO DISAGREEMENT WITH THE REPORT on count or exit code. Baseline cross-checked without a second full run rather than taken on faith: scripts/test_generate_skills_lock.py is the only test file the diff touches, and `grep -c '^def test_'` gives 161 at b81f6f1 vs 187 at HEAD = +26, so 988 - 26 = 962, exactly the stated baseline. Worktree `git status --porcelain` empty before and after my work; every attack ran against throwaway fixture registries under /tmp, and the branch was neither modified nor pushed.

defects.summary: The new federated remediation line omits --ref, so following it advances the PRIMARY pin as a side effect of a source-only repair — the exact defect class agentskills #108 already fixed for --check-format.
defects.evidence: scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:1858-1861 prints `python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --repin-source '<reg>@'`. Measured on a fixture where ONLY the source drifted (harness /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/bc2/probe.py, P1): --check-current printed one federated verdict; running exactly that command took the lock's primary ref from 60f17465 to 4bd46e75 (the checkout's HEAD) at exit 0, i.e. a content advance the verdict said had not happened. The generator already owns the anchor for this: report_digest_format prints `--ref {_suggested_repin_ref(document)}` precisely so 'the command a reviewer reads there is the command that produced the diff beneath it' (scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:1182-1196), and _agent-guidance/scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1119-1132 records the eight-lock incident that motivated it. This PR's own test knows the anchor is required: scripts/test_generate_skills_lock.py:510-531 (test_repin_source_leaves_the_primary_ref_alone_when_only_a_source_is_named) passes `--ref primary_sha` and its docstring calls that shape "The fleet bumper's federated-only night ... exactly this invocation" — yet the message that tells a human what to type omits it, and scripts/test_generate_skills_lock.py:710-713 pins the un-anchored string. The anchored form is representable and works: `--repin --ref <pin> --repin-source 'X@'` returned exit 0 with the primary held and the source advanced. Fix: emit `--ref {ref}` in the federated block when the primary is not itself in `drifted`.

defects.summary: The cross-repo contract comment (and the matching test docstring) assert a truncation-safety invariant that is demonstrably false: head -20 CAN keep a FAILED: headline and drop its remediation line.
defects.evidence: scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:1826-1831 states fact 3: "Every headline is IMMEDIATELY followed by its own remediation line. That is what makes the 20-line cap safe: a truncation can drop a whole trailing block, but it can never separate a headline from the command that fixes it." scripts/test_generate_skills_lock.py:746-751 repeats it. Counterexample measured with /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/bc2/trunc.py: a primary block is 5 fixed lines + N difference lines, so with N=14 the output is headline(1), remediation(2), notes(3-5), diffs(6-19), federated headline(20), federated remediation(21). `sed -n '/^FAILED:/,$p' | head -20` keeps line 20 and cuts line 21 — a headline separated from the command that fixes it. The named test (scripts/test_generate_skills_lock.py:744-769) only asserts adjacency in the UNTRUNCATED output (its fixture produces 12 lines), so it does not test the property the comment credits it with. Not live today — _agent-guidance/scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1360 slices only the primary-scoped, single-block run — but the comment is written as the licence a scoped per-source bumper (the report's PR 2) would rely on.

defects.summary: --only '' slips both new argparse guards because they test truthiness, so the flag is silently ignored outside --check-current instead of erroring.
defects.evidence: scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:1634 `if args.only and not args.check_current:` and :1636 `if args.only and (args.check or args.check_format):`. Measured (probe.py, P4): `--check --only '' -o <lock> --repo <dir>` exits 0 printing the normal OK line, and a plain generate with `--only ''` exits 0 writing the lock — both silently ignoring a flag the guards' own messages say only means something with --check-current. `--check-current --only ''` correctly errors (`ERROR: --only: must be OWNER/REPO or an https:// / file:// URL, got ''`). `is not None` is the check that matches the documented contract.

defects.summary: --repin-source has no skills-shrink guard and writes a smaller lock at exit 0; the report's ground for deferring that guard ("no caller passes the flag yet") is contradicted by the generator's own new remediation line.
defects.evidence: Measured (probe2.py, P5): a source federating two skills, one of whose directories is deleted at the new HEAD, re-pinned with `--repin --repin-source 'X@'` — exit 0, `Wrote …: 2 skills`, lock skills went ['adam/alpha','cms-platform/deploy','cms-platform/publish'] -> ['adam/alpha','cms-platform/deploy']. The fleet's protection against this lives only in _agent-guidance (skills_shrink_reason, scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:646+), which never passes --repin-source. The implementation report defers the guard on the grounds that "both new flags are inert unless passed and no caller passes them yet" — but scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:1858-1861 now instructs a human to pass it, so the flag has a caller from day one. (The equivalent hazard on a primary --repin is pre-existing, and an emptied source tree raises an unhandled tarfile.ReadError traceback on both the old and new generator — verified pre-existing, so not a finding against this PR.)

defects.summary: Commit 2ebef21 discharges a cross-repo debt recorded in _agent-guidance without recording the reverse debt, leaving a stale instruction over there that nothing points at.
defects.evidence: _agent-guidance/scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1134-1145 says "A SIBLING SITE MOVES WITH THIS ... agentskills' report_digest_format docstring carries a paragraph beginning 'One consequence to expect rather than re-discover' ... It is a one-paragraph edit over there — make it when that repo is next open". Verified the paragraph is now gone (`grep -n "One consequence to expect" scripts/generate_skills_lock.py` -> rc=1) and the replacement at scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:1185-1196 is accurate against bump-consumer-locks.sh:1139-1141 (`repin_ref_args=(--ref "$old_ref")` on the format branch). But that bumper block now describes an agentskills paragraph that no longer exists and tells a future reader to make an edit already made. The new comment says only "a change to either half still has to be carried across by hand" — it does not name the counterpart block, so nothing in either repo points at the now-stale instruction.

defects.summary: The scoped OK line reads the lock's raw source ref rather than the planned one and _select_sources returns every match, so the line can name a ref that is not the one read, or one of several.
defects.evidence: scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:1809 `scoped_ref = ref if include_primary else selected[0]["ref"]` takes the UNRESOLVED lock entry, while plan_sources resolves a source ref (scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:905) and the drift verdict prints the resolved one. Measured (probe.py, P3): a lock whose source ref is `main` gives `OK: the working tree still matches main (1 skills).` while the same source's FAILED headline names fa521937…. Measured (probe2.py, P7): a lock federating one registry twice under different bundles scopes to both, and the OK line reads `OK: the working tree still matches 273d637f… (2 skills).` — one ref named, two read. The comment at :1805-1808 ("there is no new way for this line to name a ref nobody checked") survives literally, but the line no longer uniquely identifies what the run looked at.
